text: {"features":[{"name":"Role motivation","description":"How specifically and convincingly the letter explains why the applicant wants this exact role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives only generic motivation and could plausibly be sent to many software roles with minimal changes."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows real interest in security or Google but explains the attraction mostly in broad, reusable terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives at least one concrete reason for wanting this role, but the motivation is only partly developed."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter offers several specific reasons tied to the team's mission, responsibilities, or scale, making the interest clearly credible."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents a clear, distinctive, and deeply role-specific motivation that feels personally grounded and hard to reuse elsewhere."}]},{"name":"Platform mindset","description":"How strongly the letter values foundational infrastructure and cross-organizational leverage.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows little or no interest in foundational systems or downstream organizational leverage."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions scale or impact in general terms but does not explain the value of core platform work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter notes central teams, foundational systems, or broad reach once, without making it a major part of the case."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly emphasizes inherited leverage, company-wide impact, or capacity multiplication as a reason for fit."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly frames past work and future goals around building core systems whose benefits compound across many teams."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"How well the letter shows a desire to help developers adopt secure practices through usable tooling and defaults.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not show meaningful interest in enabling other engineers or making secure behavior easier."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter gestures at helping others or building tools, but not in a developer-centered or workflow-aware way."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter mentions helping developers, reducing toil, or improving defaults in passing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter clearly frames security tooling as a way to support busy engineers through better defaults, routing, usability, or workflow fit."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong empathy for developer reality and repeatedly positions security engineering as making the secure path the easy path at scale."}]},{"name":"Security engineering perspective","description":"How sophisticated the letter's view of security work is as an engineering discipline.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter treats security as a generic domain label and offers no meaningful view of how security work should operate."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter states interest in security but gives little sense of security as a practical engineering discipline."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows one relevant perspective such as attacker thinking, secure defaults, lifecycle integration, or quiet resilience."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter articulates a clear view of security as systems design, automation, scalable process, or developer-facing engineering."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents a nuanced, role-relevant security philosophy that connects risk, developer behavior, scalable controls, and operational reality."}]},{"name":"Production engineering depth","description":"How much substantive experience the letter shows in testing, maintaining, and launching production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter only lightly establishes qualifying production work, with minimal scope or ownership beyond baseline requirements."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter establishes production experience but with limited scale, limited service count, or thin evidence of ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows solid multi-year experience across testing, maintaining, and launching production services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows several years of responsibility for multiple production services, including launch and ongoing operation."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents extensive production responsibility over many years and services, signaling strong readiness for a high-leverage infrastructure role."}]},{"name":"Go fluency","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates relevant Go experience for back-end system design and implementation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter names Go but offers almost no evidence of depth, ownership, or relevance to back-end responsibilities."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows regular Go use, but the evidence of depth or responsibility remains limited."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter presents Go as a main working language for production services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial Go ownership in back-end or core service work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Go central to important production systems and ties it directly to the kind of back-end ownership this role requires."}]},{"name":"Python fluency","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates relevant Python experience for tooling, automation, or services.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter omits Python or mentions it without meaningful usage context."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter presents Python as light scripting or incidental support work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows Python as a regular tool for automation, tooling, prototypes, or services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes production-grade Python with clear ownership of services, tooling, or operational systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Python central to substantial automation or agent workflows and shows reliability-minded engineering around it."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems experience","description":"How much direct experience the letter shows with agentic or autonomous systems relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of agentic or autonomous workflow experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions agents or autonomy vaguely without clarifying the applicant's role or the system design."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter indicates hands-on work with agent-like workflows at a general level."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes designing agentic systems with defined orchestration, supervision, or boundaries."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architectures and explains how permissions, auditing, or constraints were engineered."}]},{"name":"Applied AI maturity","description":"How mature the letter's evidence is for building and operating AI features in production.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows no meaningful applied AI experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI interest or exposure without concrete shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter cites shipped model-backed or LLM-based functionality."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter pairs production AI work with discussion of evaluation, reliability, or failure-mode handling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents substantial applied AI experience with concrete safeguards and clear engineering judgment about dependable deployment."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability response automation","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or related workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows no direct experience with vulnerability-handling automation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter references vulnerability reports or security queues but not building automation around them."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states direct involvement in automating vulnerability triage or intake."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes a concrete pipeline for classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong ownership of transforming manual vulnerability handling into a scalable automated workflow with explicit operational benefit."}]},{"name":"Security assessment depth","description":"How much hands-on experience the letter shows in assessing systems for security risk.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no substantive evidence of security assessment work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions reviews or assessments in vague terms without scope or method."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter indicates hands-on assessments such as threat modeling, code review, release review, or service review."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows repeated or cross-stack assessment work with a clear approach to findings and remediation."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates mature assessment practice grounded in attack surfaces, design assumptions, code reality, and validation of fixes."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"How convincingly the letter shows practical strength with algorithms and data structures.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter offers no evidence of algorithmic strength beyond generic technical competence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter claims algorithmic strength but gives no concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives one specific example of a useful structure choice or algorithmic improvement."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong practical algorithmic thinking applied to an important bottleneck or system path."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates deep algorithmic judgment through specific examples that materially changed system performance, tractability, or design simplicity."}]},{"name":"Impact evidence","description":"How clearly the letter shows the results or leverage of the applicant's work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mainly lists activities without showing what changed because of them."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter hints at benefits in broad terms but gives limited concrete effect."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states clear results such as reduced toil, faster systems, or improved routing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter ties multiple experiences to concrete operational or team impact."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently frames work in terms of measurable leverage, capacity gains, or meaningful risk reduction."}]},{"name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"How much sustained open-source contribution or maintenance responsibility the letter shows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions no open-source activity."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions occasional patches or light participation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter cites maintaining a small project or contributing fixes upstream with some regularity."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows active responsibility for reviews, releases, or community support."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates sustained stewardship of an actively used project or library with clear maintainer ownership."}]},{"name":"Security practice engagement","description":"How much the letter shows continued security skill development through certifications, competitions, or other practice outside core job duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter offers no external security development signal beyond workplace claims."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a basic certification or casual security hobby."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows either serious certification or regular competition participation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong external commitment through advanced certification, high-performing competition results, or both."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter combines advanced hands-on validation and sustained offensive practice in a way that materially strengthens the security case."}]},{"name":"Personal initiative","description":"How much self-directed engineering work outside assigned job duties the letter demonstrates.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows no self-directed building beyond normal employment."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a small side project or tinkering without depth, continuity, or clear learning value."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes a maintained personal project with a clear purpose."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows sustained independent work on technically meaningful systems or tools."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates ambitious self-driven engineering projects chosen to explore difficult systems or sharpen craft in ways relevant to the role."}]},{"name":"Communication polish","description":"How polished, precise, and readable the writing is.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent spelling, typing, or phrasing problems distract throughout and materially weaken credibility."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Noticeable errors or awkward wording recur often enough to interrupt reading."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The writing is generally clear but includes some errors or clumsy phrasing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is polished and easy to read with only minor slips."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The prose is exceptionally clean, precise, and professional, with strong control and no distracting errors."}]}]}
